results.question: At what temperature does water boil?
results.author: draft-claude, team to check
results.answer:
Water boils at $100^\circ\text{C}$ because that is the temperature at which it turns into steam. The temperature inside the Earth increases as you go deeper [S1]. The temperature at the very center of the Earth is about $5000^\circ\text{C}$ [S1].

- The expansion and contraction of minerals because of temperature changes causes weathering [S2].
- Chemical weathering happens when things like oxygen and water react with the minerals in rocks [S2].
results.example: When I boil water for tea, I see it turn into steam, which is like a small version of what happens when rocks change due to temperature.

results.question: explain why harappan civilization failed using a real world example
results.author: draft-claude, team to check
results.answer:
The Harappan civilization started to decline around 1700 BCE, and several reasons are suggested for this fall [S1]. Possible causes include floods, external invasions, deforestation, the decline of farming, and epidemics [S1].
- The decline of the agricultural sector is mentioned as a possible cause [S1].
- Epidemics are also listed as reasons for the decline [S1].
- Seals found from Harappa are also mentioned in relation to the fall [S1].

results.question: explain the harappan drainage system as a story
results.author: draft-claude, team to check
results.answer: The Harappan cities had a clever way to handle water! The waste water from the houses was let out into the **drains** [S2]. These drains were linked up with the main drain of the street [S1]. The builders made these drains out of **burnt bricks** and covered them with **stone slabs** [S1]. This system of drainage was effective even in small towns and villages [S1].
results.example: Imagine your house has a drainpipe that connects to the main sewer line outside your street, just like the Harappans did!
results.check: What materials did the Harappans use to build their drains?

results.question: I didn't understand what the Neolithic Revolution is, explain in simple words
results.author: draft-claude, team to check
results.answer:
The **Neolithic Revolution** is a big change in how people lived. It happened after the Mesolithic Age [S1]. This change was mainly about starting to **cultivate** food [S1]. People started growing their own food instead of just gathering it [S1]. This led to a big shift in human life [S1].

- People started to settle down in river valleys [S1].
- They also began to rear animals for food [S2].
- This change is called the Neolithic Revolution [S2].
results.example: Imagine moving from just finding wild berries to planting your own garden and raising a few chickens.
results.check: What is the main difference between food gathering and food production?

results.question: Who led the first excavation at Harappa?
results.author: draft-claude, team to check
results.answer:
The first excavation at Harappa was led by Daya Ram Sahni [S1].
- The Indus Valley Civilization is also known as the **Sindhu-Dihata** civilization because it was located along the banks of the Indus River and its tributaries [S1].
- The first excavations of this civilization were found in Harappa, which is why it is also called the **Harappan** civilization [S1].
- Another person, R.D. Banerjee, conducted excavations at Mohenjo-daro [S1].
